correctness.rationale: Knudson–Owens-White Definition4.2 defines the FULL strong matching complex as downward closure of all complete gradient sets obtained from total vertex orders. For the triangle-free cube Q3, an ordered vertex v contributes its oriented edge toward its unique earlier neighbor iff its descending link has exactly one vertex. This yields 24 incidence vertices. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 8!=40320 orders found 584 nonempty distinct gradients with 216 maximal four-element faces, giving exact f-vector (24,168,392,216). An independently constructed deterministic sequence performed 216 valid triangle–tetrahedron elementary free-face collapses; the residual 2-complex has 24 vertices, 168 edges and 176 triangles. Contracting a 23-edge spanning tree, 145 triangle relators each with two previously killed edges eliminate all remaining fundamental-group generators. Thus pi1=0, Euler characteristic=32, H2=Z^31; cellular Hurewicz and homology Whitehead give a wedge of 31 S^2. This is an exact finite exhaustive proof for Q3, not extrapolation to higher cubes. The source standalone verifier was inspected; independent code recreated the combinatorial certificate.

value.rationale: The full strong Morse complex is a specifically defined new canonical construction, and Q3 is the smallest nontrivial regular three-dimensional cube graph with a substantial higher-dimensional matching complex. Determining its integral *homotopy type* rather than only an Euler characteristic or a mod-2 rank gives a reusable benchmark and distinguishes it from familiar ordinary graph matching complexes. The exact finite classification is meaningful without claiming a general higher-cube theorem.
